title: Greifvorrichtung zum Greifen von ferromagnetischen Gegenständen

features.item: A housing containing a displaceable magnet and pole shoes with workpiece contact surfaces.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0023) The reference describes a gripping device with a housing that contains a magnet and a pole piece (pole shoe) with a contact surface for workpieces.

features.item: A magnet displaceable along a direction between a gripping position and a release position.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0017) The reference explicitly states that the magnet is displaceable by an actuator between an active (gripping) position and a passive (release) position.

features.item: Pole shoes attached to the housing, each with a workpiece contact surface.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0018) The reference describes a pole piece (pole shoe) with a contact surface for the objects to be gripped. It also states that the pole piece is separated from the housing by an intermediate element, implying attachment.

features.item: Pole shoes designed to guide a magnetic field portion to the workpiece contact surface.
features.quote: Magnetkräfte können dann durch den Polschuh auf den zu greifenden Gegenstand ausgeübt werden.
features.note: The quote indicates that the pole piece transmits magnetic forces to the workpiece, implying it guides the magnetic field.
features.refuted: The quote only states magnetic forces can be exerted through the pole shoe onto the object to be gripped, not that pole shoes are designed to guide a magnetic field portion to a workpiece contact surface.

features.item: A workpiece contact surface defining a contact surface angle of 170° to 190° with the displacement direction.
features.note: The reference does not specify any angle for the workpiece contact surface relative to the displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper with housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes where contact surface angle is 170° to 190° relative to displacement direction.
features.note: While the reference describes a magnetic gripper with a housing, displaceable magnet, and pole shoes, it does not mention any specific angle for the contact surface relative to the displacement direction.

features.item: A magnetic gripper system with a magnetic gripper and ferromagnetic workpiece, where magnet in gripping position presses workpiece against contact surfaces by magnetic force.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0003) The reference describes the gripping device's purpose as gripping and lifting ferromagnetic objects using a magnet, which implies magnetic force is used to hold the workpiece against the contact surfaces.

features.item: Housing extending along a longitudinal axis with displacement direction parallel to that axis.
features.note: (non-English passage at abstract) The reference states the magnet is displaceable along a longitudinal axis, and the housing contains these components, implying the housing extends along this axis.

features.item: Pole shoes with an active structure for directing the magnetic field portion.
features.quote: Magnetkräfte können dann durch den Polschuh auf den zu greifenden Gegenstand ausgeübt werden.
features.note: The reference implies the pole shoe directs magnetic forces, but it does not explicitly describe an 'active structure' for this purpose, nor does it detail specific structural features for directing the field.

features.item: An active structure with a bevel defining a bevel angle of 5° to 85° with the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0010) The reference mentions the pole shoe tapering away from the contact surface, which could imply a bevel, but it does not specify an 'active structure' or a specific bevel angle range.

features.item: An active structure with multiple projections for directing magnetic field and forming the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe an active structure with multiple projections for directing the magnetic field or forming the workpiece contact surface.

features.item: Adjacent first and second projections with a recess between them, recess depth or length deviating by at most 25% from projection length.
features.note: The reference does not describe projections or recesses with specific dimensional relationships.

features.item: A positioning device on the magnetic gripper for positioning the ferromagnetic workpiece on the contact surface.
features.note: The reference does not describe any specific positioning device for the workpiece on the contact surface.

features.item: First and second pole shoes where the magnet in gripping position makes the first pole shoe act as north pole and second as south pole.
features.note: (non-English passage at paragraph p0007) The reference mentions the magnet having a north and south pole, and the pole shoe being split into two components, but it does not explicitly state that these two components act as distinct north and south poles when the magnet is in the gripping position.

features.item: A magnet displaceable electrically, pneumatically, or mechanically between gripping and release positions.
features.quote: Zweckmäßigerweise kann der Aktor als pneumatische Kolben-Zylinder-Einheit oder als elektrischer Antrieb ausgebildet sein.
features.note: The reference explicitly states that the actuator for displacing the magnet can be a pneumatic piston-cylinder unit or an electric drive.
features.refuted: The quote describes the actuator as a pneumatic piston-cylinder unit or electric drive, but does not specify that a magnet is displaceable between gripping and release positions.

features.item: A position sensor detecting gripping position and/or release position, or a workpiece sensor detecting the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference does not mention any position sensors or workpiece sensors.

features.item: Housing with a receptacle for receiving a workpiece sensor and/or a supply line.
features.quote: Unabhängig davon kann das Gehäuse an seiner Mantelfläche Nuten zur Befestigung, beispielsweise von Sensoren, aufweisen.
features.note: The reference mentions grooves on the housing for attaching sensors, which could be considered a receptacle, but it does not specifically mention a receptacle for a workpiece sensor or a supply line.

features.item: A manipulator interface on the magnetic gripper for attaching to a manipulator.
features.note: The reference does not describe any manipulator interface.

features.item: Housing portion designed to suppress magnetic field escape, or a shielding device to at least partially prevent magnetic field escape.
features.note: The reference does not describe any features for suppressing magnetic field escape or shielding.

features.item: At least one projection with length deviating by at most 25% from the thickness of the ferromagnetic workpiece.
features.note: The reference does not describe projections or their dimensions relative to workpiece thickness.

features.item: A receptacle in the form of a groove in the housing.
features.quote: Unabhängig davon kann das Gehäuse an seiner Mantelfläche Nuten zur Befestigung, beispielsweise von Sensoren, aufweisen.
features.note: The reference explicitly mentions grooves (Nuten) on the housing for attachment.
features.refuted: The quote mentions grooves on the housing's outer surface for fastening sensors, not a receptacle in the form of a groove.

features.item: A bevel angle of 15° to 75° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: While the pole shoe is described as tapering, no specific bevel angle or range is provided.

features.item: A bevel angle of 40° to 60° between the active structure bevel and the workpiece contact surface.
features.note: While the pole shoe is described as tapering, no specific bevel angle or range is provided.

claims.quote: The invention relates to a gripping device for gripping ferromagnetic objects, with a magnet which is displaceable by an actuator between an active position for gripping the articles and a passive position.
claims.note: The reference discloses a gripping device for ferromagnetic objects, but it does not explicitly refer to 'a magnetic gripper according to claim 5' as claim 14[b] does. Claim 5 is not provided in the reference text.

claims.quote: Advantageously, the magnet can be arranged in the active position at or near a plane in which the contact surface extends. Magnetic forces can then be exerted by the pole piece on the object to be gripped.
claims.note: The reference discloses that magnetic forces are exerted on the object to be gripped when the magnet is in the active position, which corresponds to the gripping state. However, it does not explicitly state that the ferromagnetic workpiece is pressed against each workpiece contact surface.

claims.quote: According to a preferred embodiment, the magnet may be displaced away from the contact surface in the passive position, so that the magnet does not surround the pole piece or only at a distal portion of the pole piece.
claims.note: The reference discloses that in the passive position (release state), the magnet is displaced away from the contact surface, which implies that the magnetic force is not applied to the workpiece.

overall.why: The reference describes a magnetic gripping device with a displaceable magnet and pole shoes for gripping ferromagnetic objects, disclosing many core features of the subject invention, including the actuation mechanism and the general structure of the pole piece and magnet.
